courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Elementary Japanese I
courses.description: Introduction to modern Japanese with text and supplementary materials. Hiragana, katakana, and basic kanji are introduced. Weekly class hours devoted to basic sentence pattern exercises, speaking and writing practice, and creative application. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Elementary Japanese II
courses.description: Continued beginning course of modern Japanese with text and supplementary materials. Approximately 150 additional kanji are introduced. Focus on basic sentence pattern exercises, speaking and writing practice, and creative application. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, JAPN 101 or permission of the instructor.

source.text: JAPN 102. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisite, JAPN 101 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Introduction to Japanese Literature in Translation
courses.description: The major genres, aesthetic concepts, and classic and modern works of Japanese literature in English translation.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Popular Culture
courses.description: This course will examine how and why Tokyo emerged as a dominant locale in global mass culture. Students will be introduced to major figures and genres in Japanese pop culture.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Intermediate Japanese I
courses.description: Emphasis on situational expressions, mastery of basic structures, and approximately 150 new kanji. Conversation practice, reading and writing of passages, and creative application expected. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Intermediate Japanese II
courses.description: Continued emphasis on situational expressions, mastery of basic structures, and approximately 150 to 200 new kanji. Conversation practice, reading and writing of passages, and creative application expected. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Ancient and Medieval Japanese History and Culture
courses.description: This course surveys Japanese history and cultural development from the prehistoric period, rich with archaeological evidence, to the reunification of Japan in the late sixteenth century. One major topic is the mythology or and historical evidence for early state formation, including the role that Japan's long "unbroken" history plays in modern debates about national identity, xenophobia, and relations with regional neighbors. Another focus is the emergence of women's literature.

source.text: JAPN 231. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | HIST 271 .

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Early Modern Japanese History and Culture
courses.description: From the 1603 establishment of the Tokugawa Shogunate to the Meiji Restoration of 1868, Japan was ruled by the Tokugawa family in an unusual early modern federation, with a balance of power between the warrior government in Edo and the domanial governments spread across the archipelago. This resemblance of this system to the U.S. balance between federal and state power frames our examination of the early modern period.

source.text: JAPN 246. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | HIST 247 .

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Empire of Sex: Eroticism, Mass Culture, and Geopolitics in Japan, 1945-Present
courses.description: Tokyo, Japan, became the center of global pornographic culture after the United States occupation ended in 1952. This course will use film, animation, and historical texts to try to understand how and why this happened. Moreover, we will identify how this phenomenon impacted the lives of Japanese men and women.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Media Studies of Japan
courses.description: This course introduces Japanese thoughts and culture through the lens of media cultural studies, and studies socio-cultural issues of Japan through media productions and trends. We will learn about Japan's nationalism and imperialism, gender and family ideologies, post-Bubble economic misery and homelessness, memories of war, feminist and minority struggles, working culture, technology, and post-Fukushima philosophy of survival in film, commercials, print media, news, and TV shows.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Advanced Japanese I
courses.description: Advanced written and spoken Japanese introduced to students who have learned more than 500 kanji. Emphasis is placed on advanced expressions, conversation for a variety of situations, reading and writing longer texts, and approximately 150 additional kanji. Class conducted in Japanese. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Advanced Japanese II
courses.description: Second semester of third-year Japanese, continuing the study of written and spoken Japanese at the advanced level. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: The Culture of Modern, Imperial Japan, 1900-1945
courses.description: This course will examine the various expressions of cultural modernity in Japan with a focus on film, literature, and popular culture from 1900 to the end of the Pacific War.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Gateway to Mastering Japanese
courses.description: This course reviews the key grammar, vocabulary, and characters from the first three years of Japanese in preparation for the more advanced work of fourth-year elective courses.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Journalism
courses.description: Uses newspaper and magazine articles and television broadcasts to introduce journalistic writing and speech as well as contemporary social and cultural issues. Class conducted in Japanese. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Japanese Literature
courses.description: This course introduces students to the popular writing, both fiction and nonfiction, designed for mass-market consumption in contemporary Japan. Class conducted in Japanese. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Food and Culture in Japan
courses.description: Advanced Japanese course designed to develop Japanese skills and deepen appreciation of Japanese cooking. Students will develop the ability to discuss and write about topic-oriented issues in Japanese.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Making Music in Japan
courses.description: Students will learn a history of postwar Japanese music as an integral part of Japanese society and culture, and try to understand what messages each song attempts to communicate.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Manga as a Japanese Art and Culture
courses.description: This course explores contemporary Japanese language and culture through the pop cultural media of manga and anime. Topics include manga history, production, and various genres of Japanese comic books, manga.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Sports in Japanese Culture
courses.description: Introduces students to the unique Japanese cultural perspective on sports, while introducing new kanji and grammar structures and improving reading, speaking, and writing abilities.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Understanding Japanese Business Culture and Its Practice
courses.description: Students will learn about business culture in Japan, including customs and rules, in order to broaden their understanding of Japanese culture and people, while improving their language skills.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japanese Culture through Film and Literature
courses.description: This course helps students to improve their Japanese language skills while developing an understanding of Japanese culture through films and literature. Exercises include reading novels in Japanese, close observation of Japanese films, analysis of cultural context, writing summaries, and frequent discussion.

source.text: JAPN 417. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, JAPN 306 . | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Service Learning in Japanese Language
courses.description: The primary goal of this course is to prepare students to work, using the Japanese language in their desired occupation, such as in business, teaching at school, research, and so forth.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: JAPN 418. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, JAPN 306 . | HI-SERVICE, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Japan and Its Others
courses.description: As the Cool Japan Campaign products and Japanese pop-culture continue to be the first (and maybe the only) thing that the Westerners know about Japan, this course provides a deeper insight of Japan's history, culture, and reality, by introducing some of the populations and cultures that came to be considered as minorities in Japan.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Embodying Japan: The Cultures of Beauty, Sports, and Medicine in Japan
courses.description: Explores Japanese culture and society through investigating changing concepts of the human body. Sources include anthropological and history materials, science fiction, and film.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Women, Margin, Writing, and Transnational Japan
courses.description: This course explores literary and media art produced by women from various political and social margins of Japan, voiced from their transnational subjectivities. The transnational situations include: immigration, colonialism, diaspora, and international coalition as well as globalizing feminist alliance. By focusing on literature, film, and performance, this course takes an interdisciplinary approach to women's creative political statements.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Topics in Japanese Language and Literature
courses.description: Possible areas of study include popular culture, business Japanese, and Japanese-English translation. Course may be repeated for credit as topic changes. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Independent Readings in Japanese
courses.description: Permission of the department. For the student who wishes to create and pursue an independent project in Japanese under the supervision of a selected instructor. Maximum three credit hours per semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Structure of Japanese
courses.description: Introductory linguistic description of modern Japanese. For students of linguistics with no knowledge of Japanese and students of Japanese with no knowledge of linguistics.

source.text: JAPN 563. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, JAPN 102 or LING 101 . | FC-KNOWING. | LING 563 .

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Japanese Language and Literature
courses.description: Topic varies by instructor. Possible topics include Japanese literature, popular culture, and media. Course may be repeated for credit as topic changes. Participation in relevant extracurricular activities encouraged.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.
